response.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) AS overall_mean FROM per_patient) SELECT pp.SEX, AVG(pp.avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(pp.avg_diff) AS avg_of_avg_diff, AVG(pp.avg_diff / o.overall_mean) AS avg_ratio FROM per_patient pp CROSS JOIN overall o GROUP BY pp.SEX

assumptions.assumption: IGA−IGM is computed per record, so a record is skipped in that average if either IGA or IGM is NULL. The per-patient average is the mean of those record differences.
The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the per-patient IGA−IGM averages, over patients that have at least one non-null difference. It is not a record-level mean.
Patients with a NULL (not blank) SEX, if any exist, appear as their own NULL group. Blank-string SEX is a separate group.
